title: Build α-BaNaO₄ crystal structure
action: Construct the tetragonal P4/mmm unit cell of α-BaNaO₄ with Ba, Na ions and O₂ dimers arranged in head-to-head stacking along [001] separated by Ba. Write an initial structure file for DFT.
description: The α-BaNaO₄ crystal is built from the paper's explicit structural description. Lattice parameters can be approximated; the agent may refine during relaxation.

title: DFT relaxation of α-BaNaO₄
action: Perform a full geometry relaxation (atomic positions and lattice parameters) with spin‑unpolarised DFT using the PBE functional, a plane‑wave basis, and PAW pseudopotentials. Save the final relaxed structure and total energy.
description: The relaxation is carried out with Quantum ESPRESSO using a sufficiently high plane‑wave cutoff and k‑point density. The output must contain the final atomic coordinates and lattice vectors.

title: Phonon dispersion and dynamical stability
action: Run finite‑displacement phonon calculations on the relaxed structure using the PHONOPY interface with Quantum ESPRESSO. Obtain the full phonon band structure across the Brillouin zone and determine the minimum frequency.
description: The force‑constant matrix is generated by displacing atoms, and PHONOPY is used to compute phonon frequencies. The evidence file should contain the phonon dispersion data.

title: Elastic constants and mechanical stability
action: Compute the elastic stiffness constants of the relaxed α-BaNaO₄ structure from DFT stress‑strain calculations. Check that the constants satisfy the tetragonal Born stability criteria.
description: Elastic constants (C11, C12, C13, C33, C44, C66) are obtained from stress‑strain relations or energy‑strain fits. The evidence file should contain the computed constants and the boolean result of the Born criteria check.

title: Spin‑polarized DFT for magnetic configurations
action: Perform spin‑polarized DFT calculations for the FM, AFM1, AFM2, AFM3, and NM collinear arrangements of the α-BaNaO₄ cell. Extract total energies and derive nearest‑neighbour (J1) and next‑nearest‑neighbour (J2) exchange coupling constants.
description: Each calculation should use the same functional and pseudopotential settings. The evidence file must record the total energy of each configuration and the derived J1, J2 values.

title: Spin‑resolved band structure
action: Compute the spin‑resolved electronic band structure of the FM ground‑state structure along a high‑symmetry path. Determine whether the spin‑up channel is insulating (gap > 0) and the spin‑down channel is metallic (Fermi level crossed).
description: The functional can be PBE (or HSE06 if feasible). The evidence file should contain the band energies along the path for both spin channels and the extracted spin‑up gap and spin‑down metallic flag.

title: Monte Carlo simulation for Curie temperature
action: Implement a classical Heisenberg Monte Carlo simulation using the extracted J1, J2, and a magnetic anisotropy A. Compute the temperature‑dependent magnetization and magnetic susceptibility to locate the Curie temperature.
description: The simulation should use a sufficiently large supercell and adequate equilibration steps. The evidence file should contain the magnetization vs. temperature curve and susceptibility curve from which the Curie temperature is extracted.

title: Compile final results
action: Read the outputs of all previous steps and assemble a single JSON file containing: minimum gemess of phonon frequency (cm⁻¹), elastic stability boolean, magnetic ground state string, energy differences (dict), spin‑up band gap (eV), spin‑down metallic boolean, and Curie temperature (K). Write the file to /app/outputs/results.json.
description: This step collects the key quantitative findings into one artifact. The checker will read this file and compare each value against hidden paper‑derived gold standards with tolerances.
output_schema: {"minimum_phonon_frequency": <float, cm⁻¹, >0 for stable>, "elastic_stability": <bool, true if Born criteria hold>, "magnetic_ground_state": <string, "FM"|"AFM"|"NM">, "energy_differences": {"FM_vs_AFM1": <float, meV>, "FM_vs_AFM2": <float, meV>, "FM_vs_AFM3": <float, meV>, "FM_vs_NM": <float, meV>}, "spin_up_bandgap": <float, eV>, "spin_down_metallic": <bool, true if Fermi level is crossed in spin‑down channel>, "curie_temperature": <float, K>}
